summary: /messages endpoint returns every message for the user with .all() + lazy sender.name access — unbounded scan (40-60k rows for power users) with per-row relationship load. PF1 query-count test would catch the N+1 at runtime; the shape itself is the reviewable issue.

findings.message: list_all() calls .all() on a filter that scales with user history (40-60k rows for power users). Response serialization holds the whole result set + JSON tree in memory per request; multi-hundred-MB RSS and multi-second serialize time per hit.
findings.suggestion: Introduce keyset pagination: accept `?cursor=<created_at,id>` + `?limit=<50, capped at 200>`; query with `WHERE (created_at, id) < (:cursor_ts, :cursor_id) LIMIT :capped_limit`. Return cursor for next page in the payload.

findings.message: Response comprehension touches `m.sender.name` per row — SQLAlchemy will issue a lazy SELECT on senders for each message unless a joinedload/selectinload is added. Also flagged by PF1 mechanical layer (query-count would fail), but the ROOT CAUSE is the serializer shape, not the ORM.
findings.suggestion: Either (a) selectinload(Message.sender) in the query for the paginated result, or (b) return sender_id only and let the client fetch sender details in a batch endpoint.
